llm_evidence_note: No model is called. The real native ctx.terminals PTY seam is driven through a minimal BYQ-owned TerminalAttachment adapter; this is terminal-attachment-continuity evidence, NOT real-LLM-quality evidence.

ownership.rule: BYQ owns ONLY the bounded TerminalAttachment lifecycle (BYQ-minted attachment id, owner principal/authorization, runtime generation, executor epoch, state, audit). DSH owns the PTY/shell/process/IO. BYQ must not build a PTY runtime, must not copy a DSH terminal, must not build a second generic harness and must not persist or fake the native PTY.

required_scenarios.description: generation A establishes a real native persistent terminal plus a durable BYQ TerminalAttachment; the BYQ adapter OS process is aborted and a fresh adapter generation B loads the SAME durable attachment, authorizes and generation-validates, finds the native state still reachable and rebinds the SAME attachment / native session / PTY pid with no replay and no loss

the BYQ adapter restart in the committed topology also takes the native DSH runtime with it; a fresh adapter generation loads the SAME durable attachment, performs authorization and generation validation, finds the native process-local state genuinely unreachable, deterministically reports lost/interrupted and rejects a fake reattach. Per ADR-0083 this honest state is the acceptance, and the observer must distinguish it from a not-implemented/label-only PASS

optional_scenarios.description: host reboot. NOT executed: rebooting the maintainer host is not authorized and a container/adapter/process restart is not a host reboot.

required_cross_checks.description: the BYQ attachment is a real durable, BYQ-minted record distinct from any DSH session id or pid: it persists to a BYQ-owned store, carries owner principal + runtime generation + executor epoch + state + audit linkage, and reloads with the same id in a fresh adapter OS process
an owner/principal boundary cannot be bypassed: a foreign principal presenting the attachment is rejected, and a different native owner cannot read or send to another owner's PTY
a stale runtime generation / executor epoch is fenced before any rebind decision; the current generation/epoch still rebinds or honestly fails
an unknown/wrong attachment or terminal id is rejected and cannot reach a real PTY
re-attach and close are idempotent: repeating a valid reattach returns the same identity without creating a second native session, and closing twice is a no-op with the same state
closing the attachment ends the native PTY and runtime shutdown leaves no orphan shell process

fail_closed: required scenario not covered by a PASS
a required scenario PASS without the exact dimensions and derived identity honesty
a required scenario PASS without fault_applied when the contract requires a fault
a required cross-check with a false assertion
an honest-lost scenario that does not prove the native state is genuinely gone
a positive rebind that is not exercised, i.e. a label-only PASS that never rebinds a durable attachment
a negative that was not rejected
a false reattach (session/attachment/pid changed but identity_stable claimed)
any attempt by the observation to declare its own coverage/continuity rules

notes.native_seam: the real native @deepseek-ai/dsh-terminal service + @deepseek-ai/dsh-terminal-bash backend own the PTY/shell/IO; a minimal BYQ adapter owns only the durable TerminalAttachment lifecycle. No PTY runtime, no second generic harness, no DSH fork/patch.
notes.adapter_restart: the BYQ adapter OS process is SIGKILLed; a fresh adapter OS process reloads the durable store. Native sessions are process-local, so when the adapter restart also ends the native runtime the honest result is lost/interrupted, never a fabricated reattach.
notes.reachability_rule: the positive rebind is required to prove the lifecycle is implemented, so a not-implemented/label-only loss cannot pass.
notes.host_reboot: kept separate and NOT_RUN in this batch
notes.scope: candidate/qualification layer only; no production selector switch, no R4 productization, no raw DSH schema in any browser/frontend surface
